# 1. Overview

This is the fifth of six notebooks for Extended Data Fig 1 (see
`4_build_plant_tree.Rmd`). It converts the **HOSTS** host-record dataset into the
butterfly species by plant genus associations shown in the figure and writes
them, together with the per-genus and per-species annotations, to
`../output_data/host_matrix/` for use by `6_plot_host_matrix_figure.Rmd`.

The record cleaning and plant-taxonomy standardization follow the pipeline of
`Figure_2/code/Blanca_HOSTS_milkweed_asclepias_ASR.Rmd`, ensuring that Extended
Data Fig 1 and Figure 2 rest on the same curated set of associations. The
procedure comprises the following steps:

1. The HOSTS Danainae export is read, quality-filtered, and standardized to a
   consistent plant taxonomy.
2. Records are collapsed to butterfly species by plant genus associations, with
   the number of supporting records (`n_records`) retained for each pair.
3. The two outgroup species *Mechanitis polymnia* and *Heliconius erato* are
   incorporated from `HOSTS_Mechanitis_Heliconius.csv` (which shares the HOSTS
   schema). Neither feeds on Apocynaceae or Moraceae, so both appear as empty
   rows in the figure.
4. Two curation rules are applied. Under the **native-range rule**, an *Asclepias*
   association is counted only where the butterfly's native range overlaps that
   of *Asclepias* (`native_range_overlap == "yes"`). Under the **single-record
   rule**, a single-record association that constitutes a butterfly's only
   evidence for the milkweed clade, or its only evidence for *Asclepias*, is
   retained only if it has been manually validated in
   `HOSTS_single_record_milkweed_associations_BH.csv`; single-record milkweed
   associations for butterflies with additional milkweed evidence are retained
   without such validation.
5. The associations are restricted to Apocynaceae and Moraceae, the plant
   families shown in the figure, and the resulting associations and annotations
   are written to disk.

```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(ape)

in_dir  <- "../input_data/host_matrix"
out_dir <- "../output_data/host_matrix"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- small helpers (from Blanca_HOSTS_milkweed_asclepias_ASR.Rmd) ---
clean_name <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(as.character(x), "_", " "))
}
blank_to_na <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_squish(as.character(x))
  dplyr::na_if(x, "")
}

# Plant families shown in the figure
FIGURE_PLANT_FAMILIES <- c("Apocynaceae", "Moraceae")
# Milkweed-clade subfamilies (Asclepias belongs to Asclepiadoideae)
MILKWEED_SUBFAMILIES  <- c("Asclepiadoideae", "Secamonoideae")
```

# 2. Read the HOSTS records

Both the main Danainae export and the outgroup workbook share the HOSTS column
schema, so a single function maps raw HOSTS columns to the tidy per-record
schema used downstream.

```{r hosts-schema}
# Map a raw HOSTS-schema data frame (CSV or Excel sheet) to the tidy schema.
hosts_schema <- function(raw) {
  raw %>%
    transmute(
      butterfly_family     = blank_to_na(Family),
      butterfly_subfamily  = blank_to_na(Subfamily),
      butterfly_genus      = clean_name(Genus),
      butterfly_epithet    = clean_name(Species),
      butterfly_subspecies = blank_to_na(Subspecies),
      plant_genus_original = clean_name(Plantgenus),
      plant_species        = blank_to_na(Plantspecies),
      plant_family_original = blank_to_na(`APG plantfamily`),
      country              = blank_to_na(Country),
      source               = blank_to_na(Source),
      secondary_source     = blank_to_na(`Secondary source`),
      date                 = blank_to_na(Date),
      captive_flag         = blank_to_na(`Captive?`),
      error_flag           = blank_to_na(`Error?`),
      natural_host_flag    = blank_to_na(`Nathost?`)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      butterfly_species = str_squish(paste(butterfly_genus, butterfly_epithet))
    )
}

# Quality filters used by the original HOSTS curation: drop records with missing
# or uncertain butterfly names, missing plant genera, or captive/error/
# non-natural-host flags.
quality_filter <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(butterfly_genus),
      !is.na(butterfly_epithet),
      !str_detect(butterfly_species, "\\?"),
      !is.na(plant_genus_original),
      !captive_flag %in% c("?", "Y"),
      !error_flag %in% c("?", "O", "Y"),
      !natural_host_flag %in% "N"
    )
}
```

```{r read-main-hosts}
hosts_raw <- read.csv(
  file.path(in_dir, "HOSTS_Danainae.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "NA")
)

hosts <- hosts_schema(hosts_raw) %>%
  mutate(record_id = paste0("hosts_", row_number()), .before = 1)

hosts_filtered <- quality_filter(hosts)

cat("Raw HOSTS records:        ", nrow(hosts), "\n")
cat("After quality filters:    ", nrow(hosts_filtered), "\n")
cat("Records removed:          ", nrow(hosts) - nrow(hosts_filtered), "\n")
```

# 3. Standardize plant genera and add taxonomy

The POWO-based recoding and the plant taxonomy table are taken verbatim from
`Blanca_HOSTS_milkweed_asclepias_ASR.Rmd` so the two figures resolve plant
taxonomy identically. The original HOSTS genus is retained for traceability.

```{r plant-taxonomy}
standardize_hosts <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    left_join(powo_recode, by = "plant_genus_original") %>%
    mutate(plant_genus = coalesce(plant_genus, plant_genus_original)) %>%
    left_join(
      plant_taxonomy,
      by = c("plant_family_original" = "plant_family", "plant_genus"),
      suffix = c("", "_taxonomy")
    ) %>%
    rename(plant_family = plant_family_original) %>%
    select(
      record_id, butterfly_family, butterfly_subfamily, butterfly_genus,
      butterfly_epithet, butterfly_subspecies, butterfly_species,
      plant_family, plant_subfamily, plant_tribe, plant_subtribe,
      plant_genus, plant_genus_original, plant_species, country, source,
      secondary_source, date
    )
}

hosts_standardized <- standardize_hosts(hosts_filtered)
cat("Standardized records:", nrow(hosts_standardized), "\n")
```

# 4. Integrate the outgroups (*Mechanitis polymnia*, *Heliconius erato*)

`HOSTS_Mechanitis_Heliconius.csv` holds the *Mechanitis* and *Heliconius* host
records in the HOSTS column schema. We keep only the two species that are tips in
the Danaini tree and run them through the same cleaning / standardization used
above.

```{r read-outgroups}
outgroup_raw <- read.csv(
  file.path(in_dir, "HOSTS_Mechanitis_Heliconius.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "NA")
)

outgroup_tips <- c("Mechanitis polymnia", "Heliconius erato")

outgroup_standardized <- outgroup_raw %>%
  hosts_schema() %>%
  mutate(record_id = paste0("outgroup_", row_number()), .before = 1) %>%
  quality_filter() %>%
  filter(butterfly_species %in% outgroup_tips) %>%
  standardize_hosts()

cat("Outgroup records kept:\n")
print(count(outgroup_standardized, butterfly_species))

records <- bind_rows(hosts_standardized, outgroup_standardized)
```

# 5. Collapse to butterfly species x plant-genus associations

Every pair supported by at least one record is retained; `n_records` counts the
distinct records supporting each pair.

```{r associations}
associations <- records %>%
  group_by(
    butterfly_family, butterfly_subfamily, butterfly_genus, butterfly_species,
    plant_family, plant_subfamily, plant_tribe, plant_subtribe, plant_genus
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_records = n_distinct(record_id),
    countries = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(country))), collapse = "; "),
    sources   = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(source))), collapse = "; "),
    secondary_sources = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(secondary_source))),
                              collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(countries, sources, secondary_sources), ~ na_if(.x, "")))

cat("Associations (>= 1 record):", nrow(associations), "\n")
cat("...supported by a single record:", sum(associations$n_records == 1), "\n")
```

The full association set (`associations`) is retained for the per-species
host-use states exported for the ancestral state reconstruction (Section 11),
which must cover every species the reconstruction might place on its tree. The
figure itself shows only the species that are tips in the Danaini tree
(`Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick`); a tree-restricted copy, `assoc_tree`, is used for the
figure matrix and scopes the single-record validation (Section 7) to the
butterflies that are actually plotted.

```{r restrict-to-tree}
tree_tips <- clean_name(read.tree(file.path(in_dir, "Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick"))$tip.label)

cat("All species with associations:", n_distinct(associations$butterfly_species), "\n")
cat("Tree tips:", length(tree_tips), "\n")
cat("Tree tips with no associations (empty rows in figure):",
    paste(setdiff(tree_tips, associations$butterfly_species), collapse = ", "),
    "\n")
```

# 6. Native-range *Asclepias* coding

```{r biogeography}
overlap_lut <- read.csv(
  file.path(in_dir, "butterfly_plant_biogeography.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(butterfly_species = clean_name(butterfly_species)) %>%
  distinct(butterfly_species, native_range_overlap)

associations <- associations %>%
  left_join(overlap_lut, by = "butterfly_species")

# Tree-scoped copy used for the figure matrix and the single-record validation.
assoc_tree <- associations %>%
  filter(butterfly_species %in% tree_tips)
```

# 7. Single-record validation against the BH dataset

A single-record association needs manual validation only when that one record is
the butterfly's **sole** evidence for the milkweed clade or its **sole** evidence
for *Asclepias* -- i.e. only then does keeping or dropping it change whether the
butterfly is scored as a milkweed / *Asclepias* user. Per-butterfly evidence
counts are taken over the full association set (a non-native *Asclepias* record
still counts as milkweed-clade evidence, matching Figure 2's coding), while a
non-native *Asclepias* record is excluded from the "must-validate" set because
the native-range filter (Section 8) removes it before it can be plotted.

The validated associations live in
`HOSTS_single_record_milkweed_associations_BH.csv`. If any qualifying case is
*not* in that file, the notebook stops so the BH file can be updated.

```{r single-record-gate}
bh_validated <- read.csv(
  file.path(in_dir, "HOSTS_single_record_milkweed_associations_BH.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "NA")
) %>%
  transmute(
    butterfly_species = clean_name(butterfly_species),
    plant_genus       = str_squish(plant_genus)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(butterfly_species), butterfly_species != "") %>%
  distinct()

# Per-butterfly evidence counts (over the tree-scoped associations)
evidence_counts <- assoc_tree %>%
  group_by(butterfly_species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_milkweed  = sum(plant_subfamily %in% MILKWEED_SUBFAMILIES),
    n_asclepias = sum(plant_genus == "Asclepias"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

qualifying <- assoc_tree %>%
  left_join(evidence_counts, by = "butterfly_species") %>%
  filter(
    n_records == 1,
    plant_genus == "Asclepias" | plant_subfamily %in% MILKWEED_SUBFAMILIES
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sole_milkweed   = plant_subfamily %in% MILKWEED_SUBFAMILIES & n_milkweed == 1,
    sole_asclepias  = plant_genus == "Asclepias" & n_asclepias == 1,
    # non-native Asclepias is dropped in Section 8, so never needs validation
    survives_native = !(plant_genus == "Asclepias" &
                        !(native_range_overlap %in% "yes")),
    must_validate   = (sole_milkweed | sole_asclepias) & survives_native,
    in_bh = paste(butterfly_species, plant_genus) %in%
            paste(bh_validated$butterfly_species, bh_validated$plant_genus)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(must_validate), butterfly_species, plant_genus)

write.csv(
  qualifying %>%
    select(butterfly_species, plant_family, plant_subfamily, plant_genus,
           n_records, n_milkweed, n_asclepias, native_range_overlap,
           sole_milkweed, sole_asclepias, must_validate, in_bh),
  file.path(out_dir, "Ext_fig1_single_record_to_verify.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

to_validate <- qualifying %>% filter(must_validate)
cat("Single-record cases requiring BH validation:", nrow(to_validate), "\n")
print(to_validate %>%
        select(butterfly_species, plant_genus, sole_milkweed, sole_asclepias,
               native_range_overlap, in_bh))

missing_from_bh <- to_validate %>% filter(!in_bh)
if (nrow(missing_from_bh) > 0) {
  stop(
    "These sole-evidence single-record associations are not validated in ",
    "HOSTS_single_record_milkweed_associations_BH.csv:\n",
    paste0("  - ", missing_from_bh$butterfly_species, " -> ",
           missing_from_bh$plant_genus, collapse = "\n")
  )
}
cat("All qualifying single-record cases are validated in the BH file.\n")
```

# 8. Apply the curation rules and build the present-association table

```{r present-associations}
# Pairs to drop: sole-evidence single-record milkweed/Asclepias associations not
# validated in BH (none remain after the Section 7 guard, but applied defensively).
drop_pairs <- qualifying %>%
  filter(must_validate, !in_bh) %>%
  transmute(key = paste(butterfly_species, plant_genus))

present_associations <- assoc_tree %>%
  # native-range Asclepias filter
  filter(!(plant_genus == "Asclepias" & !(native_range_overlap %in% "yes"))) %>%
  # drop unvalidated sole-evidence single records
  filter(!(paste(butterfly_species, plant_genus) %in% drop_pairs$key)) %>%
  # restrict to the plant families shown in the figure
  filter(plant_family %in% FIGURE_PLANT_FAMILIES) %>%
  mutate(
    present    = 1L,
    tile_state = if_else(plant_genus == "Asclepias", "Asclepias", "Present")
  ) %>%
  # native_range_overlap is a species-level attribute used only to filter
  # Asclepias cells above; it is not written out, since on a per-association row
  # it would be easily misread as describing that row's plant.
  select(butterfly_species, plant_family, plant_subfamily, plant_genus,
         n_records, present, tile_state)

cat("Present associations (Apocynaceae + Moraceae):", nrow(present_associations), "\n")
cat("...Asclepias cells:", sum(present_associations$plant_genus == "Asclepias"), "\n")

write.csv(
  present_associations,
  file.path(out_dir, "Ext_fig1_host_associations.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 9. Plant-genus annotations (taxonomy + cardenolides)

`known_cardenolide` is a genus-level attribute taken from
Karageorgi et al. (2019); subfamily/family come from the standardized
taxonomy. Genera with no cardenolide record are coded 0 (absent/unknown).

```{r plant-annotations}
cardenolide_lut <- read.csv(
  file.path(in_dir, "plant_butterfly_long_all.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(plant_genus = str_squish(plant_genus)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(plant_genus), plant_genus != "") %>%
  group_by(plant_genus) %>%
  summarise(known_cardenolide = max(as.integer(known_cardenolide), na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(known_cardenolide = if_else(is.finite(known_cardenolide),
                                     known_cardenolide, 0L))

plant_genus_attributes <- present_associations %>%
  distinct(plant_genus, plant_family, plant_subfamily) %>%
  left_join(cardenolide_lut, by = "plant_genus") %>%
  mutate(known_cardenolide = replace_na(known_cardenolide, 0L)) %>%
  arrange(plant_family, plant_subfamily, plant_genus)

cat("Plant genera in figure:", nrow(plant_genus_attributes), "\n")
cat("...with known cardenolides:",
    sum(plant_genus_attributes$known_cardenolide == 1), "\n")

write.csv(
  plant_genus_attributes,
  file.path(out_dir, "Ext_fig1_plant_genus_attributes.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 10. Butterfly ATPα annotations

The ATPα state of each butterfly species is drawn from
Karageorgi et al. (2019), the same source used for Figure 2. Only resolved
states are retained; species without a resolved state are rendered as "unknown"
in the figure. 

```{r atpa}
butterfly_atpa <- read.csv(
  file.path(in_dir, "plant_butterfly_long_all.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    butterfly_species = clean_name(butterfly_species),
    atpa_state        = na_if(str_squish(atpa_state), "")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(butterfly_species), butterfly_species != "",
         !is.na(atpa_state), atpa_state != "unknown") %>%
  group_by(butterfly_species) %>%
  summarise(atpa_state = first(atpa_state), .groups = "drop")

# Outgroup genotype not recorded in Karageorgi et al. (2019)
butterfly_atpa <- butterfly_atpa %>%
  filter(butterfly_species != "Heliconius erato") %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(butterfly_species = "Heliconius erato", atpa_state = "QAN"))

cat("Butterfly species with a resolved ATPalpha state:", nrow(butterfly_atpa), "\n")

write.csv(
  butterfly_atpa,
  file.path(out_dir, "Ext_fig1_butterfly_atpa.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 11. Per-species host-use states for ancestral state reconstruction

The ancestral state reconstruction in
`Figure_2/code/Blanca_HOSTS_milkweed_asclepias_ASR.Rmd` operates on a single
host-use state per species rather than on individual associations. That table is
produced here, so the reconstruction can read it directly instead of rebuilding
the associations from the raw records. Each species' ATPα state (Section 10) is
appended as a final column; species without a resolved ATPα state are left `NA`.

The states follow Figure 2's coding exactly and are therefore derived from the
**full integrated association set** (`associations`), *before* the figure-specific
filters of Section 8. In particular, a non-native *Asclepias* record still counts
as use of the Asclepiadoideae/Secamonoideae clade here, whereas it is dropped from
the plotted matrix:

- `asclepias` -- the species has an *Asclepias* association whose native range
  overlaps *Asclepias* (`native_range_overlap == "yes"`);
- `Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae` -- otherwise, the species uses any
  Asclepiadoideae or Secamonoideae genus (including non-native *Asclepias*);
- `none` -- no association in the Asclepiadoideae/Secamonoideae clade.

The two-state coding collapses this to native-range *Asclepias* use versus none.
Because every sole-evidence single-record Asclepiadoideae/Secamonoideae/*Asclepias*
association is validated in the BH file (Section 7), these states are identical
whether or not the single-record gate is applied, and the table covers every
species with at least one host record.

```{r host-use-states}
host_use_states <- associations %>%
  group_by(butterfly_species) %>%
  summarise(
    has_asclepias             = any(plant_genus == "Asclepias"),
    has_asclepias_native      = any(plant_genus == "Asclepias" &
                                    native_range_overlap %in% "yes"),
    has_asclepiad_secamonoid  = any(plant_subfamily %in% MILKWEED_SUBFAMILIES),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    host_use_3state = case_when(
      has_asclepias_native     ~ "asclepias",
      has_asclepiad_secamonoid ~ "Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae",
      TRUE                     ~ "none"
    ),
    host_use_2state = if_else(has_asclepias_native, "asclepias", "none")
  ) %>%
  # add the ATPalpha state (Section 10); species without a resolved state are NA
  left_join(butterfly_atpa, by = "butterfly_species") %>%
  arrange(butterfly_species)

cat("Species with a host-use state:", nrow(host_use_states), "\n")
cat("Three-state counts:\n");  print(table(host_use_states$host_use_3state))
cat("Two-state counts:\n");    print(table(host_use_states$host_use_2state))

write.csv(
  host_use_states,
  file.path(out_dir, "danaini_host_use_states.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
